meta.title: Prism — Local-first frontend observability
meta.description: A local-first frontend observability platform. Session replay, diagnostic signals, multi-window alignment — your data stays on your machine. No cloud, no lock-in.

hero.sub: Prism is a local-first frontend observability platform. Session replay, diagnostic signals, multi-window alignment — error / console / network interleaved into one timeline. Scrub to second 3 and see the page, that console.error, and that 500 — together.
hero.foot: REC · observer-sdk one-line integration · single-binary self-host

pain.eyebrow: The pain · The three costs of cloud RUM
pain.h2_mid: and what you pay isn't money — it's
pain.sub: Mainstream session-replay tools upload user data to a third-party cloud by default, bill per session, and use proprietary formats. Privacy, cost, lock-in — three costs, and you pay all three.

c1.title: User sessions uploaded to a third-party cloud
c1.desc: Every click, input, and network request is sent to someone else's server. Finance, healthcare, government — unacceptable by default.

c2.title: Billed per session — the more you use, the more you pay
c2.desc: per-session / per-seat pricing. When traffic spikes, the bill explodes instead of scaling. Exporting your own data means talking to sales.

c3.title: Your data isn't in your hands
c3.desc: Sessions are vendor-hosted in proprietary export formats — migration cost is huge. When prices rise, service stops, or terms change, you have no fallback.

manifesto.h2_pre: Your data stays in your hands —

b1.d: A session is just a JSON file on your own disk. It never touches a third-party server; no port is opened to the cloud.

b2.t: Local is the default, not an option
b2.d: Runs with zero cloud dependency. Self-hosted private cloud is an opt-in topology, not the only path. A tool you don't own your data in isn't a tool.

b3.d: No alerts, no RUM metrics, no funnels or heatmaps. We focus on one diagnostic loop: reproduce → understand → annotate → share.

b4.d: prism-session is a plaintext JSON spec, shared across local files / local server / cloud upload. Take it with you anytime; delete it clean anytime.

capabilities.sub: From capture to deploy, six capabilities you can explain in one sentence — each maps to a real mechanism in the product, not marketing copy.

c1.title: Local-first, data never leaves
c1.desc: Zero cloud dependency by default. User data never touches a third-party server — privacy-compliant by construction, no vendor lock-in.

c2.title: Multi-window aligned recording — exclusive
c2.desc: Tauri multi-window shares a wall clock; replay syncs multiple tracks. The core argument for desktop-app debugging — no one else does this.

c3.title: Interleaved event model
c3.desc: error / console / network interleave into the DOM event stream as type:6, sharing one timeline — no cross-stream alignment needed.

c4.title: Diagnosis-oriented, not monitoring
c4.desc: No alerts, no RUM metrics. Focus on the reproduce → understand → annotate → share diagnostic loop.

c5.title: Single-binary self-host
c5.desc: observer-server — one file hosts API + frontend together. Air-gapped networks, offline, compliance audits all work.

c6.title: Open bundle contract
c6.desc: prism-session — a plaintext JSON spec shared across local / server / cloud paths. Take it with you anytime.

compare.sub: It's not a feature-count comparison — it's a difference in positioning. Cloud RUM ships your data out and bills per session; Prism keeps your data and does one thing: diagnosis.

architecture.sub: No magic. The recording base is open-source rrweb 2; storage and server are independent Rust crates; cross-process migration follows a plaintext JSON contract. Every layer is readable, auditable, and replaceable.

quickstart.sub: Embed it in any web app, or run a self-hosted server. Fully open source, data in your hands.

sdk.label: Embed in your app
sdk.s3: records offline, replays when back online

quickstart.foot: MIT · Rust core + Vue console + Web SDK · fully open source

multiwindow.sub: Each Tauri desktop window runs its own rrweb recorder, with events carrying absolute timestamps on a shared clock. On replay, shown/hidden intervals drive each segment in sync along the main timeline — main window, settings panel, modal. Three tracks aligned. No one else does this.
multiwindow.ctrl_hint: Click a track to scrub · multi-window shared playhead
multiwindow.foot: Traditional replay: single window, single stream · Prism: shown/hidden intervals drive sync, multi-track aligned

diagnosis.sub: Scrub to second 3 and see the page, that console.error, and that 500 — together. Traditional RUM scatters them across Network / Logs / Errors tabs; Prism lets them explain themselves on one axis.
diagnosis.foot: Traditional RUM: jump across three tabs, times don't line up · Prism: one axis, self-explanatory
diagnosis.frame_empty: Waiting for events to enter the window…

loop.sub: One chain runs the whole diagnostic flow: recording captures DOM + diagnostic signals, replay aligns multiple tracks, diagnosis makes sense of it, annotations leave marks, and export ships a single-file bundle to share. Every step in one tool.

s4.label: Annotate
s4.desc: Session-level annotations, separate from the event stream

deploy.sub: One core codebase, three deployment forms: a desktop app with zero cloud dependency, a single-binary self-host, or pure-browser with zero install. From solo developers to enterprise intranets, pick the topology you need — your data stays in your hands.

f1.title: Tauri 2 desktop app
f1.desc: macOS / Windows / Linux, zero cloud dependency. A local analysis console, ready out of the box, data written to appDataDir.

f2.desc: One binary hosts both the API and the console frontend. --web-dir enables the SPA, bind 0.0.0.0 to expose it publicly, with multi-tenant quotas.

f3.title: Pure-browser access
f3.desc: The console runs entirely in the browser — enter your endpoint + key at LoginGate and go. No install; HttpBackend talks directly to your self-hosted server.

footer.tag_suf: Your data stays in your hands — no cloud, no lock-in.
